theory.intro: The **mode** of a continuous random variable is the value of $x$ at which the density $f(x)$ is greatest. It is the peak of the graph, found by solving $f'(x)=0$ or by checking an endpoint.
facts: Solve $f'(x)=0$, then confirm the point is a maximum with $f''(x)<0$ or a sign table.
Reject any stationary point outside the support, because $X$ cannot take that value.
If $f'(x)>0$ throughout the support the density is increasing, so the mode is the right endpoint $b$.
If $f'(x)<0$ throughout the support the density is decreasing, so the mode is the left endpoint $a$.
Compare $f$ at every stationary point and at both endpoints, because the largest value wins.
steps: Solve $f'(x)=0$ and keep only the roots inside the support.
Compare $f$ at those roots and at both endpoints; the largest value gives the mode.

development.solution_text:
$f'(x)=\frac{3x^{2}-48x+180}{2688}$
$3x^{2}-48x+180=0$
$x^{2}-16x+60=0$
$(x-6)(x-10)=0$
$x=6$ or $x=10$
$x=10$ is rejected because it lies outside $[0,8]$.
$f''(x)=\frac{6x-48}{2688}$
$f''(6)=\frac{-12}{2688}<0$, so $x=6$ is a maximum.
$f(0)=0$, $f(6)=\frac{432}{2688}$ and $f(8)=\frac{416}{2688}$.
The mode is $6$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$}, xmin=-1, xmax=9.4, ymin=-0.03, ymax=0.22, samples=100, clip=false, width=8cm, height=6cm, xtick={0,2,4,6,8}, ytick={0.05,0.1,0.15}]
\addplot[thick, domain=0:8] {(x*x*x-24*x*x+180*x)/2688};
\draw[dashed] (axis cs:6,0) -- (axis cs:6,0.1607);
\node[above] at (axis cs:6,0.175) {mode $=6$};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

$f'(x)=\frac{10-2x}{54}$
$10-2x=0$
$x=5$
$x=5$ is rejected because it lies outside $[6,9]$.
With no stationary point in the support, $f'(x)=\frac{10-2x}{54}<0$ for every $x$ in $[6,9]$.
The density is decreasing, so the maximum is at the left endpoint.
$f(6)=\frac{24}{54}$ and $f(9)=\frac{9}{54}$.
The mode is $6$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$}, xmin=-1, xmax=10.6, ymin=-0.07, ymax=0.6, samples=100, clip=false, width=8cm, height=6cm, xtick={0,2,4,6,8}, ytick={0.2,0.4}]
\addplot[thick, domain=6:9] {(10*x-x*x)/54};
\draw[dashed] (axis cs:6,0) -- (axis cs:6,0.4444);
\node[above right] at (axis cs:6,0.47) {mode $=6$};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

$f'(x)=\frac{3x^{2}-18x+24}{116}$
$3x^{2}-18x+24=0$
$x^{2}-6x+8=0$
$(x-2)(x-4)=0$
$x=2$ or $x=4$
$x=2$ is rejected because it lies outside $[3,7]$.
$f''(x)=\frac{6x-18}{116}$
$f''(4)=\frac{6}{116}>0$, so $x=4$ is a minimum, not a maximum.
$f(3)=\frac{19}{116}$, $f(4)=\frac{17}{116}$ and $f(7)=\frac{71}{116}$.
The largest value is at the right endpoint.
The mode is $7$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$}, xmin=-0.6, xmax=8.4, ymin=-0.09, ymax=0.8, samples=100, clip=false, width=8cm, height=6cm, xtick={0,2,4,6}, ytick={0.2,0.4,0.6}]
\addplot[thick, domain=3:7] {(x*x*x-9*x*x+24*x+1)/116};
\draw[dashed] (axis cs:7,0) -- (axis cs:7,0.6121);
\node[above left] at (axis cs:7,0.65) {mode $=7$};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

mastery.solution_text:
$f(x)=\frac{3}{1024}(8x^{2}-x^{3})$
$f'(x)=\frac{3}{1024}(16x-3x^{2})$
$\frac{3}{1024}x(16-3x)=0$
$x=0$ or $x=\frac{16}{3}$
$f''(x)=\frac{3}{1024}(16-6x)$
$f''(0)=\frac{48}{1024}>0$, so $x=0$ is a minimum.
$f''\left(\frac{16}{3}\right)=\frac{3}{1024}(16-32)<0$, so $x=\frac{16}{3}$ is a maximum.
$f(0)=0$, $f\left(\frac{16}{3}\right)=\frac{2}{9}$ and $f(8)=0$.
The mode is $\frac{16}{3}$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$}, xmin=-1, xmax=9.4, ymin=-0.04, ymax=0.3, samples=100, clip=false, width=8cm, height=6cm, xtick={0,2,4,6,8}, ytick={0.1,0.2}]
\addplot[thick, domain=0:8] {3*x*x*(8-x)/1024};
\draw[dashed] (axis cs:5.3333,0) -- (axis cs:5.3333,0.2222);
\node[above] at (axis cs:5.3333,0.24) {mode $=\frac{16}{3}$};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

$\frac{5x^{4}}{32}\ge 0$ for every $x$ in $[0,2]$.
$\int_{0}^{2}\frac{5x^{4}}{32}\,dx=\left[\frac{x^{5}}{32}\right]_{0}^{2}$
$=\frac{32}{32}$
$=1$
So $f$ is a probability density function.
$f'(x)=\frac{5x^{3}}{8}$
$f'(x)>0$ for $0<x\le 2$, so $f$ is increasing across the support.
The mode is $2$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$}, xmin=-0.4, xmax=3.2, ymin=-0.36, ymax=3.1, samples=100, clip=false, width=8cm, height=6cm, xtick={0,1,2}, ytick={1,2}]
\addplot[thick, domain=0:2] {5*x*x*x*x/32};
\draw[dashed] (axis cs:2,0) -- (axis cs:2,2.5);
\node[above left] at (axis cs:2,2.6) {mode $=2$};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
